answer: One concrete defense is tying each agent's earning power to a verifiable work history. Like a cedar that only grows rings over real seasons, an agent accumulates a reputation ledger that a fresh sybil copy lacks. The ledger acts like an opal: its value comes from the layered, hard-to-fake pattern of past behavior, not a single claim. A newcomer may join, but its rewards start small and only grow as its pigment of genuine activity deepens, so spinning up thousands of empty identities costs more than it earns.
